The Chapter on the Coupling 2.10.
The Discourse on Emptiness
Thus have I heard:
at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
As the Venerable Ānanda was sitting to one side, he said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, it is said, ‘The world is empty, the world is empty.
In what way, venerable sir, is it said that ‘the world is empty’?”
“Because, Ānanda, it is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, therefore it is said: ‘The world is empty.
And of what, Ānanda, is it empty of a self or of what belongs to a self?
The eye, Ānanda, is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.”
Forms are empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
Eye-consciousness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
Eye-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
Whatever feeling— whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant— arises conditioned by eye-contact, that too is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
The ear is empty … [and so on] … sounds are empty …
The nose is empty...
odors are empty...
the tongue is empty...
Tastes are empty...
the body is empty...
tangibles are empty...
The mind is empty of a self or of anything belonging to a self.
Mental phenomena are empty of a self or of anything belonging to a self.
Mind-consciousness is empty of a self or of anything belonging to a self.
“Mind-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
Whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.
Because it is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, Ānanda, it is said: ‘The world is empty.’”
10.1. The Matrix:

Emptiness of emptiness, emptiness of formations, emptiness of change, supreme emptiness, emptiness of characteristics, emptiness by suppression, emptiness by substitution of opposites, emptiness by cutting off, emptiness by tranquillization, emptiness by escape, and internal emptiness.

Emptiness externally, emptiness of both, emptiness of the similar, emptiness of the dissimilar, emptiness of seeking, emptiness of grasping, emptiness of acquisition, emptiness of penetration, emptiness of unity, emptiness of diversity, emptiness of acceptance, emptiness of determination, and emptiness of thorough investigation;
the exhaustion of the occurrence of one who is clearly comprehending is the ultimate emptiness among all forms of emptiness. [25]
10.2. Exposition. What is the emptiness of emptiness?
The eye is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, of permanence, of stability, of eternity, or of anything not subject to change.
The ear is empty … the nose is empty … the tongue is empty …
The body is empty … the mind is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, of permanence, of stability, of eternity, or of anything not subject to change.
This is the emptiness of emptiness.
What is the emptiness of formations?
There are three formations:
the formation of merit, the formation of demerit, and the formation of the imperturbable.
The formation of merit is empty of the formation of demerit and the formation of the imperturbable.
The formation of demerit is empty of the formation of merit and the formation of the imperturbable.
The formation of the imperturbable is empty of the formation of merit and the formation of demerit.
These are three formations.
There are another three formations:
the bodily formation, the verbal formation, and the mental formation.
The bodily formation is empty of the verbal formation and the mental formation.
The verbal formation is empty of the bodily formation and the mental formation.
The mental formation is empty of the bodily formation and the verbal formation.
These are three formations.
There are another three formations:
past formations, future formations, and present formations.
Past formations are empty of future and present formations.
Future formations are empty of past and present formations. Present formations are empty of past and future formations.
These are the three kinds of formations.
This is the emptiness of formations.
What is the emptiness of change?
Form that has arisen is empty of intrinsic nature.
Form that has passed away is both changed and empty.
Feeling that has arisen is empty of intrinsic nature.
Feeling that has passed away is both changed and empty... [and so on]...
Perception has arisen… volitional formations have arisen… consciousness has arisen…
The eye that has arisen … [and so on] … existence that has arisen is empty of its own intrinsic nature.
Existence that has passed away is both changed and empty.
This is emptiness through change.
What is the supreme emptiness?

This is the foremost state, this is the best state, this is the most distinguished state, namely: the stilling of all formations, the relinquishing of all acquisitions, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.
This is the foremost emptiness.
What is the emptiness of characteristics?
There are two characteristics:
The characteristic of a fool and the characteristic of a wise person.
The characteristic of a fool is empty of the characteristic of a wise person;
the characteristic of a wise person is empty of the characteristic of a fool.
There are three characteristics:
the characteristic of arising, the characteristic of vanishing, and the characteristic of change while standing.
The characteristic of arising is empty of both the characteristic of vanishing and the characteristic of change while standing.

The characteristic of subsidence is empty of the characteristic of arising and the characteristic of change-while-standing; the characteristic of change-while-standing is empty of the characteristic of arising and the characteristic of subsidence.
The characteristic of arising of material form is empty of the characteristic of subsidence and the characteristic of change-while-standing;
the characteristic of subsidence of material form is empty of the characteristic of arising and the characteristic of change-while-standing.
The characteristic of the alteration of what has endured in form is empty of the characteristic of arising and the characteristic of passing away.
[It is the same for] feeling … perception … [and so on].
...of volitional formations ...
of consciousness ...
of the eye ...
The characteristic of arising of aging-and-death is empty of the characteristic of passing away and the characteristic of change-while-standing.
The characteristic of passing away of aging-and-death is empty of the characteristic of arising and the characteristic of change-while-standing.
The characteristic of change-while-standing of aging-and-death is empty of the characteristic of arising and the characteristic of passing away.
This is the emptiness of characteristics.
What is the emptiness by suppression?
Through renunciation, sensual desire is both suppressed and empty.
By means of non-ill will, ill will is both suppressed and empty.
By means of the perception of light, sloth and torpor are both suppressed and empty.
By means of non-distraction, restlessness is both suppressed and empty.
Through the discernment of phenomena, doubt is both suppressed and voided.
Through knowledge, ignorance is both suppressed and voided.
Through gladness, discontent is both suppressed and voided.
By means of the first jhāna, the hindrances are both suppressed and empty...
[and so on] ...by means of the path of arahantship, all defilements are both suppressed and empty.
This is suppression-emptiness (*vikkhambhana-suñña*).
What is emptiness by way of its own constituent part (*tadaṅga-suñña*)?
Sensual desire is empty of itself by way of renunciation;
ill will is empty of itself by way of non-ill will.
Through the perception of light, sloth and torpor are empty by way of their specific factor.
Through non-distraction, restlessness is empty by way of its specific factor.
Through the discernment of phenomena, doubt is empty by way of its specific factor.
By means of knowledge, ignorance is empty of its own part.
By means of gladness, discontent is empty of its own part.
By means of the first jhāna, the hindrances are empty of their own parts …pe…
In the contemplation of turning away, the adherence to fetters is empty by way of their specific factor;
this is emptiness by way of specific factor (*tadaṅga-suñña*).
What is emptiness by way of eradication (*samuccheda-suñña*)?
Through renunciation, sensual desire is both eradicated and empty.
Through non-ill will, ill will is both eradicated and empty.
Through the perception of light, sloth and torpor are both eradicated and empty.
Through non-distraction, restlessness is both completely eradicated and empty.
Through the discernment of phenomena, doubt is both completely eradicated and empty.
Through knowledge, ignorance is both completely eradicated and empty.
By means of joy, discontent is both eradicated and empty.
By the first jhāna, the hindrances are both eradicated and empty …pe… by the path of arahantship, all defilements are both eradicated and empty.
This is emptiness by eradication.
What is emptiness by subsiding? Through renunciation, sensual desire has both subsided and become empty.
Through non-ill will, ill will is both stilled and empty.
Through the perception of light, sloth and torpor are both stilled and empty.
Through non-distraction, restlessness is both stilled and empty.
Through the discernment of phenomena, doubt is both stilled and voided.
Through knowledge, ignorance is both stilled and voided.
Through gladness, discontent is both stilled and voided.
By means of the first jhāna, the hindrances are both stilled and empty ... [and so on] ...
by means of the path of arahantship, all defilements are both stilled and empty.
This is the emptiness of subsiding (*paṭippassaddhi-suñña*).
What is emptiness as escape? Through renunciation, sensual desire is both escaped from and empty.
Through non-ill will, ill will is both escaped from and empty.
Through the perception of light, sloth and torpor are both escaped from and empty.
Through non-distraction, restlessness is both escaped from and empty.
Through the discernment of phenomena, doubt is both escaped from and empty.
By means of knowledge, ignorance is both escaped from and empty of.
By means of gladness, discontent is both escaped from and empty of.
By means of the first jhāna, the hindrances are both escaped from and empty of … [and so on] …
By means of the path of arahantship, all defilements have both departed and are empty.
This is emptiness as escape.
What is internal emptiness?
The internal eye is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, of permanence, of stability, of eternity, or of anything not subject to change.
The internal ear is empty...
the internal nose is empty...

The internal tongue is empty … the internal body is empty … the internal mind is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, of permanence, of stability, of eternity, or of anything subject to changelessness.
This is internal emptiness.
What is external emptiness?
External forms are empty … [and so on] …
External phenomena are empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, of permanence, of stability, of eternity, or of anything that is not subject to change.
This is emptiness regarding the external.
What is emptiness regarding both?
The internal eye and external forms—both of these are empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, of permanence, of stability, of eternity, or of anything not subject to change.
The internal ear and external sounds...
[and so on] ...the internal nose and external odors...
Whatever is the internal tongue and whatever are external tastes...
whatever is the internal body and whatever are external tangibles...

whatever is the internal mind and whatever are external mental phenomena—both of these are empty of a self or of anything belonging to a self, of anything permanent, stable, eternal, or of a nature that does not change.
This is the voidness of both.
What is the voidness of the similar?
The six internal sense bases are both similar and void.
The six external sense bases are both similar and empty.
The six groups of consciousness are both similar and empty.
The six groups of contact are both similar and empty.
The six classes of feeling are both similar and empty.
The six classes of perception are both similar and empty.
The six classes of volition are both similar and empty.
This is the emptiness of the similar.
What is the emptiness of the dissimilar?
The six internal sense bases are both dissimilar to and empty of the six external sense bases.
The six external sense bases are both dissimilar to and empty of the six groups of consciousness.
The six groups of consciousness are both dissimilar to and empty of the six groups of contact.
The six groups of contact are both dissimilar to and empty of the six groups of feeling.
The six groups of feeling are both dissimilar to and empty of the six groups of perception.
The six groups of perception are both dissimilar to and empty of the six groups of volition.
This is "dissimilarity-emptiness."
What is emptiness regarding searches? The search for renunciation is empty of sensual desire;
the search for non-ill will is empty of ill will.
The search for the perception of light is empty of sloth and torpor.
The search for non-distraction is empty of restlessness.
The search for the discernment of phenomena is empty of doubt.

The seeking for knowledge is empty of ignorance. The seeking for joy is empty of discontent. The seeking for the first jhāna is empty of the hindrances … and so on … [up to] … the seeking for the cessation of suffering is empty of the origin of suffering. The seeking for the path is empty of the wrong path. The seeking for the fruit is empty of the non-fruit. The seeking for Nibbāna is empty of all formations. The seeking for seclusion is empty of the non-secluded. The seeking for detachment is empty of attachment. The seeking for cessation is empty of arising. The seeking for relinquishment is empty of grasping. The seeking for the deathless is empty of the mortal. The seeking for the unconditioned is empty of the conditioned. The seeking for the signless is empty of signs. The seeking for the desireless is empty of desires. The seeking for emptiness is empty of the perception of self. The seeking for the void is empty of the perception of being.

The seeking for the base of infinite space is empty of the base of infinite consciousness. The seeking for the base of infinite consciousness is empty of the base of nothingness. The seeking for the base of nothingness is empty of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. The seeking for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is empty of the attainment of cessation. The seeking for the attainment of cessation is empty of the attainment of identity. The seeking for the Dhamma is empty of the non-Dhamma. The seeking for the Discipline is empty of what is not the Discipline. The seeking for the True Dhamma is empty of the counterfeit Dhamma. The seeking for the great sovereignty over the great sovereignty over the powers is empty of the states contrary to the powers’ mastery. The search for the path of arahantship is empty of all defilements.
This is emptiness in terms of searching.
What is emptiness in terms of encompassing?
The embracing of renunciation is empty of sensual desire.
The embracing of non-ill will is empty of ill will.
The embracing of the perception of light is empty of sloth and torpor.
The comprehension of non-distraction is empty of restlessness.
The comprehension of the definition of phenomena is empty of doubt.
The comprehension of knowledge is empty of ignorance.
The embracing of gladness is empty of discontent.
The embracing of the first jhāna is empty of the hindrances …pe… the embracing of the path of arahantship is empty of all defilements.
This is emptiness of possession.
What is emptiness of acquisition?
The acquisition of renunciation is empty of sensual desire.
The attainment of non-ill will is empty of ill will.
The attainment of the perception of light is empty of sloth and torpor.
The attainment of non-distraction is empty of restlessness.
The attainment of the discernment of phenomena is empty of doubt.
The attainment of knowledge is empty of ignorance.
The attainment of gladness is empty of aversion.
The attainment of the first jhāna is empty of the hindrances...
[and so on] ...the attainment of the path of arahantship is empty of all defilements.
This is emptiness by way of attainment.
What is emptiness as penetration?
Penetration of renunciation is empty of sensual desire.
Penetration of non-ill will is empty of ill will.
The penetration of the perception of light is empty of sloth and torpor.
The penetration of non-distraction is empty of restlessness.
The penetration of the discernment of phenomena is empty of doubt.
The penetration of knowledge is empty of ignorance.
The penetration of gladness is empty of discontent.
The penetration of the first jhāna is empty of the hindrances … [and so on] …
The penetration of the path to arahantship is empty of all defilements; this is the emptiness of penetration (*paṭivedha-suñña*).
What is the emptiness of unity (*ekatta-suñña*) and the emptiness of diversity (*nānatta-suñña*)?
Sensual desire is diversity; renunciation is unity.
For one who intends the unity of renunciation, it is empty of sensual desire.
Ill will is diversity; non-ill will is unity.
For one intending unity through non-ill will, it is empty of ill will.
Drowsiness and lethargy are diversity; perception of light is unity.
For one intending unity through perception of light, it is empty of drowsiness and lethargy.
Restlessness is diversity; non-distraction is unity.
For one who intends with non-distraction as unity, there is emptiness of restlessness.
Doubt is diversity; the discernment of phenomena is unity.
For one who intends the unity of the discernment of phenomena, it is empty of doubt.
Ignorance is diversity; knowledge is unity.
For one who intends the unity of knowledge, it is empty of ignorance.
Discontent is diversity; gladness is unity.
For one who intends gladness as unity, there is emptiness of discontent.
The hindrances are diversity; the first jhāna is unity.
For one who intends the unity of the first jhāna, it is empty of the hindrances...
[and so on] ...all defilements are diversity; the path of arahantship is unity.
For one who intends the unity of the path of arahantship, it is empty of all defilements.
This is emptiness of unity and emptiness of diversity.
What is emptiness of acceptance?
Acceptance of renunciation is empty of sensual desire.
The patience of non-ill will is empty of ill will;
the patience of perception of light is empty of sloth and torpor;
the patience of non-distraction is empty of restlessness.
The patience of discerning phenomena is empty of doubt.
The patience of knowledge is empty of ignorance.
The patience of gladness is empty of discontent.
The acceptance of the first jhāna is empty of the hindrances …pe… the acceptance of the path of arahantship is empty of all defilements.
This is emptiness of acceptance.
What is the emptiness of resolution?
Resolution upon renunciation is empty of sensual desire.
Resolution upon non-ill will is empty of ill will.
The foundation of the perception of light is empty of sloth and torpor.
The foundation of non-distraction is empty of restlessness.
The foundation of the discernment of phenomena is empty of doubt.
The foundation of knowledge is empty of ignorance.
The foundation of gladness is empty of discontent.
The foundation of the first jhāna is empty of the hindrances … and so on …
The resolution upon the path of arahantship is empty of all defilements.
This is the emptiness of resolution.
What is the emptiness of fathoming?
The pervasion of renunciation is empty of sensual desire.
The pervasion of non-ill will is empty of ill will.
The pervasion of the perception of light is empty of sloth and torpor.
The penetration of non-distraction is empty of restlessness.
The penetration of the discernment of phenomena is empty of doubt.
The penetration of knowledge is empty of ignorance.
The pervasion of gladness is empty of discontent.
The pervasion of the first jhāna is empty of the hindrances …pe… the pervasion of the path of arahantship is empty of all defilements.
This is the emptiness of thorough investigation.
What is the ultimate emptiness among all forms of emptiness—the exhaustion of the occurrence of one who is clearly comprehending?
Here, one who is clearly comprehending brings the occurrence of sensual desire to its end through renunciation, and the occurrence of ill will through non-ill will.
It exhausts the occurrence of sloth and torpor by means of the perception of light;
it exhausts the occurrence of restlessness by means of non-distraction; it exhausts the occurrence of doubt by means of the discernment of phenomena;
it exhausts the occurrence of ignorance by means of knowledge; it exhausts the occurrence of discontent by means of gladness; by the first...
By means of jhāna, the occurrence of the hindrances is exhausted … [and so on] … by means of the path of arahantship, the occurrence of all defilements is exhausted. Alternatively,

for one who possesses clear comprehension and is attaining final nibbāna in the element of nibbāna without residue, this very occurrence of the eye is exhausted, and no other occurrence of the eye arises.
This very occurrence of the ear … [and so on] … the occurrence of the nose … the occurrence of the tongue …
The occurrence of the body...
the occurrence of the mind is exhausted, and no further occurrence of the mind arises.
This is the exhaustion of occurrence for one who is clearly comprehending; it is the ultimate emptiness among all forms of emptiness.
The Discourse on Emptiness is finished.
This is the second chapter, the Chapter on the Coupling.
Its summary verse:
The yoke-and-fettered truths and enlightenment factors,
loving-kindness with dispassion as the fifth,
the analytical knowledges, and the Wheel of Dhamma—
"Supreme powers and emptiness.
This peerless, second, excellent, and most sublime group was established by those who uphold the Nikāyas.
